Commodity vol extremes: Chicago Fed, 'The Aftermath of the 2026 Oil Shock' (https://www.chicagofed.org/publications/chicago-fed-letter/2026/523); Vanguard, 'Oil shock complicates central bank outlooks' (https://corporate.vanguard.com/content/corporatesite/us/en/corp/vemo/oil-shock-complicates-central-bank-outlooks.html); WisdomTree, 'Gold and Silvers' Most Volatile Day' (https://www.wisdomtree.com/us/insights/blog/gold-and-silvers-most-volatile-day); Bold Precious Metals, 'Gold & Silver Market Volatility February 2026 Deep Dive' (https://www.boldpreciousmetals.com/news/gold-silver-market-volatility-february-2026). Mechanism: Frazzini & Pedersen (2014), 'Betting Against Beta', J. Financial Economics 111(1); Blitz & van Vliet (2007), 'The Volatility Effect', J. Portfolio Management.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_UUP_63
rationale: Structural/policy configuration, not a track-record claim -- I make no assertion about how the dollar, UUP, or any trend strategy has recently performed, and a sign rule takes both directions, so nothing here is a directional bet. THE MECHANISM. A trailing-sign trend rule has something to capture only if the asset's dominant driver is serially correlated. For a trade-weighted dollar index that driver is the relative short-rate path against the euro and the yen, which together are roughly 71% of the six-currency ICE USDX basket UUP's index is built on (EUR ~57.6%, JPY ~13.6% at the basket's fixed 1999 weights; UUP holds long USDX futures via the DB Long USD Currency Portfolio Index, not spot). That driver is serially correlated by institutional design rather than by accident: policy rates move in 25bp increments, at scheduled meetings roughly eight times a year, preceded by forward guidance and quarterly projection rounds, and every one of these committees explicitly values gradualism -- so a change in relative stance is a multi-meeting sequence, not a single repricing. The IMF's own decomposition of dollar dynamics finds the policy-divergence (neutral-rate) shock's effect on the dollar is both substantial and PERSISTENT, working mainly through future expected short rates. Persistence in the driver is the necessary condition for a sign rule; whether it survives into tradable serial correlation in the price is the empirical question the gates decide. WHY THE CURRENT CONFIGURATION MAKES THIS A TWO-SIDED TEST RATHER THAN A DISGUISED LONG-DOLLAR BET, which is the load-bearing part. All three major central banks have now exited the 2024-25 easing cycle, and they exited in different directions relative to the US: the ECB hiked its deposit rate 25bp to 2.25% on 2026-06-11 and held there in July; the BoJ hiked in June and held at 1.0% on 2026-07-31, its highest policy rate since September 1995, while warning core inflation will exceed its 2% target; and the Fed held the target range at 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29 for a fifth consecutive meeting. So the two heaviest basket counterparts are actively normalizing UPWARD into a frozen US front end -- the differential that dominates this index is compressing from a wide starting point. At the same time the US side's own next move has flipped sign inside the committee: three presidents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) dissented in favour of a HIKE, the first time since September 2016 that three policymakers dissented with a unified view of direction. Both legs of the differential are therefore live in both directions over the OOS window, which is exactly the sample a sign rule needs to be judged on honestly. WEAKNESSES, STATED FIRST RATHER THAN APPENDED. (1) The strongest prior is directly against this candidate and is specifically about exchange rates, specifically out-of-sample: Meese & Rogoff (1983) found no macro model -- interest-differential models included -- beats a random walk out of sample at horizons up to a year, and the subsequent literature has largely sustained that. If it holds, this dies at gate 1 and should. (2) Trend is the deadest family in this lab: tsmom_*, tsmom_gen_*, donchian_*, green_line_200d are all DEAD, and a currency ticker does not earn a lower bar for being new. (3) There is a real confound between trend and carry here. UUP is a long-USD FUTURES position, so its roll embeds the very short-rate differential the mechanism above rests on; under the forward-premium puzzle (Fama 1984) that roll has an average drift of its own, and a sign rule that is long the dollar most of the time would collect it while looking like trend. That confound is the second most likely reason this deserves to die, and neither this primitive nor the gates separate the two components. (4) UUP charges an expense ratio against a futures basket and tracks the DB index, not spot DXY. (5) The 2018-present OOS window contains both the favourable realisations (the 2018 and 2022 dollar runs, sustained moves a sign rule holds) and the worst ones (March 2020's spike-and-collapse, and extended range-bound chop, where a sign rule pays the whipsaw twice). PARAMETERS, DERIVED NOT SEARCHED. lookback=63 trading days is one quarter, which spans two FOMC meetings and two ECB monetary-policy Governing Council meetings (both ~8/yr) and one full quarterly projection round (the Fed's SEP, the ECB's staff projections) -- the shortest window over which a change in relative policy STANCE is observable as a sequence rather than as one meeting's surprise, and no longer than that. freq=W because a 63-day sign can flip on any session, and a monthly clock would act up to ~21 trading days late on a 63-day signal -- a third of the signal's own horizon -- whereas weekly keeps the execution lag under ~8% of it, at turnover a quarterly-horizon sign rule rarely triggers anyway. DISTINCTNESS. No graveyard.csv row is a single-ticker UUP strategy: the DEAD tsmom_*/tsmom_gen_* families trend all 15 UNIVERSE tickers as one ensemble, where UUP is 1/15 of the book and its own signal is netted against fourteen others, so a UUP-only trend has never been isolated. In this ledger the currency asset class is the least represented of the five -- UUP has appeared in exactly one prior proposal, rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_UUP_a (a static reserve-rotation spread, now DEAD in graveyard.csv), and never as a trend leg -- and the three prior single_asset_trend proposals are GLD_126, SLV_63 and VNQ_126, all commodity or real estate. Under-used primitive and untouched asset class, motivated by a policy configuration that is live right now.

name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_VNQ_DBC_189_63
rationale: Structural configuration, not a track-record claim -- I assert nothing about how VNQ, DBC, real assets or any trend strategy has recently performed, and both legs are two-sided sign rules, so nothing here is a directional bet. THE MECHANISM I EXPECT TO MAKE THE TWO LEGS OFFSET, which is what this primitive requires me to name specifically. A nominal Treasury yield decomposes into a real yield and an inflation breakeven. VNQ and DBC are both real assets, but each is levered to a DIFFERENT term of that decomposition, and with opposite sign. Listed REITs are long-duration claims on lease-based cash flows, so their discount rate is the REAL yield: a rise in real yields re-rates them down more or less mechanically, independent of what inflation is doing. Broad commodities are the physical goods whose spot prices ARE a large part of the headline inflation the BREAKEVEN prices; DBC is an energy-heavy basket (WTI, Brent, heating oil, RBOB, natural gas, alongside metals and grains), so it trends with the inflation impulse itself. That gives two distinct, opposite-signed transmission channels rather than one inverse relationship: (a) a SUPPLY-driven inflation shock raises commodity prices directly (DBC leg trends up) while passing into headline inflation, raising nominal and then real policy-rate expectations, which is a headwind to the rate-sensitive real estate leg (VNQ trends down); (b) a DEMAND/growth slowdown does the reverse -- commodity demand and prices fall (DBC down) while real yields fall and REITs' stable, lease-based, largely domestic cash flows re-rate up (VNQ up). Because the two channels are different economic shocks rather than a single common factor with a sign flip, this is not a mechanical inverse pair, and its offsetting behaviour is conditional on which shock dominates. That distinction is the whole point: a mechanically anti-correlated pair would be one position wearing two tickers, whereas two channels that dominate in different regimes is what a hedge is supposed to look like -- and it is also why I expect this to clear the calibration-window decorrelation cap rather than fail it as a disguised single bet, since 2007-2017 contained both shock types (the 2008 demand collapse, the 2010-11 commodity boom, the 2014-15 oil-supply bust, and the whole disinflationary REIT re-rating) rather than one regime repeated. WHY THIS CONFIGURATION IS LIVE RIGHT NOW, which is what makes the two channels currently distinguishable rather than an abstraction. The market is presently pricing exactly channel (a), and pricing it as a term-structure phenomenon rather than a level one: the 10-year breakeven sits around 2.24-2.28% (July 2026), squarely inside the 2.0-2.6% band it has held since 2024, while the 5-year breakeven is roughly 18bp ABOVE the 10-year -- an inverted breakeven curve. That inversion is the precise signature of a near-term supply shock priced in with long-run anchoring intact, which is the state in which the two legs should diverge most. The supply shock is identified and dated: conflict-driven disruption of the Strait of Hormuz cut global supply sharply, lifting Brent about 65% (~$46/bbl) by end-March 2026 -- the largest monthly rise on record -- with further tanker attacks and strikes in early July 2026, and the EIA revising its 2026 Brent average from $58 to $79 in a single month. Meanwhile the 10-year TIPS real yield is around 2.3%, historically high, so the REIT leg's discount rate is under pressure at the same moment the commodity leg's driver is spiking. Sell-side framing of the same configuration is explicit that supply-driven inflation skews the risk toward DELAYED Fed easing, 'limiting support for rate-sensitive, cyclical sectors such as Financials and Real Estate', while noting REITs are relatively well positioned in lower-growth, higher-uncertainty states -- i.e. the same two channels, named by someone else. I am NOT proposing to trade that view: the candidate takes whatever sign each leg's own trailing return gives it. The current configuration matters only as evidence that the two channels are economically real and currently separable, which is the claim this primitive asks me to make and have checked. WEAKNESSES, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN APPENDED. (1) The dominant prior is against this: trend is the deadest family in this lab -- tsmom_*, tsmom_gen_*, donchian_*, green_line_200d are all DEAD against these same gates -- and combining two trend legs does not create edge that neither leg has. If both legs are individually unpredictable, pairing them produces a lower-variance nothing, which gate 1's DSR/CPCV test should and will reject. (2) The hedge argument is about RISK, not return; doctrine gate 2 asks whether a candidate earns its place, and a candidate whose only virtue is decorrelation is exactly the case the unapproved v1.1 diversifier clause would have been needed to rescue -- it is not approved, so this must clear the bar on its own. (3) DBC is a futures-basket ETF: its return embeds roll yield, so a leg that is long commodities much of the time collects or pays contango/backwardation independent of trend, and neither this primitive nor the gates separate the two. (4) VNQ's rate sensitivity is a well-known factor exposure, so the REIT leg may be a levered duration bet in disguise rather than a real-estate one. (5) The 2018-present OOS window contains the March 2020 shock, where both legs collapsed together and the claimed offset would have failed exactly when it mattered -- the single most likely way this dies for the right reason. PARAMETERS, DERIVED NOT SEARCHED. lookback_a=189 trading days (~9 months) for VNQ: cap-rate and discount-rate re-rating in listed real estate works through three quarterly reporting cycles and lags the rate move that causes it, so a window shorter than that reads noise and one at the 252 cap averages the re-rating away. lookback_b=63 (one quarter) for DBC: energy supply shocks pass into prices and into headline inflation within weeks, so the commodity leg's driver operates on a much faster clock than the real estate leg's -- the mismatch is the mechanism, not a fitted choice. freq=W is set by the FASTER leg: a 63-day sign can flip on any session, and a monthly clock would act up to ~21 trading days late on it (a third of that leg's own horizon), while weekly holds the lag under ~8%. Turnover cost is bounded regardless of cadence because a sign that does not flip generates no trade. DISTINCTNESS. No graveyard.csv row pairs real estate against commodities: the DEAD tsmom_*/ tsmom_gen_* families trend all 15 UNIVERSE tickers as a single ensemble in which VNQ and DBC are 1/15 each and net against thirteen others, so this two-leg structure has never been isolated. In this ledger the three prior asset_class_trend_hedge proposals are SPY/GLD, TLT/DBC and SPY/IEF -- every one of them anchors on an equity or rates leg, and none touches real_estate, which is the asset class with the fewest appearances here. The one prior VNQ proposal, rp_single_asset_trend_VNQ_126, is a different primitive at a different lookback, and rp_static_spread_carry_VNQ_IEF_a is a static always-on spread with no trend component; neither leg of this candidate duplicates an existing spec. Chosen partly for that breadth -- asset_class_trend_hedge is under-used (3 of 21 prior proposals against static_spread_carry's 6) -- but the mechanism above is the reason, not the tally.

name: rp_curve_carry_63
rationale: The 2s10s slope's two drivers have split onto different clocks in 2026, which is what makes a slope-momentum signal structurally interesting right now rather than a generic trend bet. The front end is being pulled down by a Fed easing toward a 3.0-3.5% funds rate over the course of 2026, a slow and largely pre-announced path; the long end is being held up by fiscal supply and term-premium normalization, which arrives in discrete bursts on the quarterly refunding calendar (the August 2026 refunding is $125bn of 3s/10s/30s including $25bn of 30-year, raising ~$28.7bn of new cash). The result on 2026-08-04 is 2y 4.21% / 10y 4.63% / 30y 5.20% -- a 2s10s of only ~42bp, far below the 100-150bp of a normal expansion, with the ACM 10-year term premium at 0.79% on 2026-07-30, clearly positive for the first time since 2023. A slope repriced by supply absorption moves in refunding-cycle-length steps, not smooth macro drift, so the pre-registered horizon here is 63 trading days -- one full quarterly refunding cycle -- measuring the change in slope across a complete supply cycle rather than intra-cycle auction noise. Monthly rebalance because a signal that only refreshes on a quarterly cadence has nothing to say at finer resolution, and the DV01-neutral TLT/IEF construction earns a small duration-differential that faster turnover would swamp. Distinct from rp_curve_carry_126 (W, proposed earlier on 2026-08-06), which spans two refunding cycles at weekly resolution and therefore averages across exactly the cycle boundary this spec is built to sit on. Honest prior: this lab has killed every predictive strategy it has tested, and curve_carry is trend-following applied to a slope rather than a price -- the reason to test it is that its input is a real macro-structural series with a named, currently-operating supply mechanism, not that trend-following deserves another look.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_EEM_EFA_a
rationale: Structural, not a track-record claim -- and the strongest current fact I found cuts AGAINST the trade, which is why it is stated in the middle rather than buried. This is the first use of EEM anywhere in this pipeline ledger and the first attempt in this lab at the emerging-market equity risk premium: graveyard.csv contains no EEM row at all, and the only prior roster appearance of the pair is family N's pre-registered EFA/EEM cointegration test, which FAILED the ADF stationarity filter on 2007-2017 (beta 0.826, ADF p=0.551) and therefore never traded OOS. THE PREMIUM. A fixed, always-on long EEM / short EFA is the canonical harvest direction of the segmentation/country-risk premium: emerging equity markets are only partially integrated with world capital markets, so their cost of equity carries a country-risk component -- political, expropriation, capital-control, institutional and local-liquidity risk -- that developed markets' does not, and country-risk measures predict future equity returns in emerging markets and NOT in developed ones, which is the empirical signature of that segmentation. The spread is paid for bearing that risk, with no directional forecast of either leg -- the same shape as this lab's one surviving carry book (crypto funding), where the return is compensation for a real tail risk rather than a prediction. WHY EFA IS THE SHORT LEG AND NOT SPY. Both legs are USD-unhedged foreign equity, so the common dollar-versus-foreign-currency beta partially cancels and what is left is closer to a clean EM-versus-developed-ex-US claim rather than a disguised short-dollar bet; and it avoids shorting the record US mega-cap AI concentration that an earlier proposal in this same ledger (rp_static_spread_carry_IWM_SPY_a) identified as contaminating any SPY short leg. THE STRUCTURAL BACKDROP, stated as backdrop and explicitly NOT as the premium: the IMF's 2026 WEO puts advanced-economy growth at 1.8% for 2026 against 3.8% for emerging market and developing economies (recovering to 4.5% in 2027), and EM entered this cycle with more monetary easing room after the 2021-22 tightening and lower public-debt ratios than DM, where policy rates are constrained by debt dynamics. Faster growth is a forecast, not a risk premium, and no part of this candidate's claim rests on it; it matters only because a segmentation premium is harder to argue is compensation for distress when the distress is not visibly increasing. THE FACT THAT CUTS AGAINST IT, and the single strongest reason this candidate may deserve to die: MSCI EM is no longer a diversified emerging-risk basket. As of 2026-06-18 the index is Taiwan 27.01%, Korea 24.87%, China 18.67%, India 10.68% -- Taiwan and Korea alone are over 51%, IT is close to 37% of the index, and Taiwan semiconductors are 16.2% on their own; Korea passed China for the first time during 2026 on a semiconductor-driven index reweighting. So long EEM / short EFA is in substance TWO bets: long a country-risk premium, and long a concentrated semiconductor and AI-hardware block against a diversified developed-ex-US index. Only the first is a risk premium; the second is an idiosyncratic sector bet this construction never intended to take, and it is the exact mirror of the concentration problem already identified on SPY's side in this ledger. The hypothesis actually under test is therefore narrower and more honest than 'does EM pay a premium': does a segmentation premium survive being levered onto a two-country semiconductor concentration? The wide EM valuation discount (MSCI EM forward P/E around 11.6 at 2026-01-01, quoted near 14x on 2026 estimates elsewhere) is cited as a SYMPTOM of that composition and of the segmentation discount itself, never as a cheapness signal -- there is no valuation timing in this construction. KNOWN NEGATIVE RUNNING COST, up front. EEM's expense ratio is roughly 0.7% against roughly 0.32% for EFA, so about 38bp/yr of any premium is paid away in fund fees before a single unit of risk is compensated, and EM dividend withholding is heavier than DM's on top of that. Unlike a mechanically-paid funding rate, this premium has to clear a known fee drag first. THE HONEST PRIOR. EM underperformed developed markets for most of the 2010s, so the modern-era record of this exact spread is against it, and I am not appealing to any more recent stretch to argue otherwise -- doing so would be the selection-on-results this ledger exists to avoid. The OOS window (2018-present) contains at least three episodes that should punish this construction hard if the premium is not real: the 2018 dollar and trade-war drawdown, March 2020, and the 2021-22 China regulatory crackdown and property bust, all cases where EM fell further than DM. If the average premium does not survive those net of the fee drag above, gate 1's DSR against a duty-cycle-matched null or gate 3's pain test should kill it; that is the hypothesis under test, not a caveat appended to a bullish case. ON PRIMITIVE CHOICE, since static_spread_carry is the most-used primitive in this ledger (6 of 23 rows) and breadth is preferred: the two under-used primitives were both worse choices TODAY, not by default. curve_carry (2 uses) has a one-dimensional parameter space and already received two proposals within the last four hours (lookback 126 and 63) -- a third lookback today would be an LLM-run parameter sweep of a single mechanism, exactly the multiple-testing shape DOCTRINE.md warns about. cross_sectional_rank (3 uses) has had each of its three metrics proposed within the last 30 hours, and its low_vol arm is the most exhaustively factory-swept mechanism in graveyard.csv (roughly 30 low_vol_xsec_gen_* verdicts spanning 16d to 179d lookbacks, every one DEAD with negative OOS Sharpe). The research I actually did supports a structural carry claim, and static_spread_carry is its only home in the current vocabulary. freq M matches a static spread whose only turnover is the rebalance back to fixed weights.

name: rp_curve_carry_252
rationale: The 2s10s slope's current re-steepening is driven by two structurally distinct, slow-moving forces that push the same way and both run on a multi-quarter clock, not a meeting-to-meeting one. (a) The front end is being pulled down by a measured, multi-year easing cycle -- 175bp of cuts since Sep 2024 to a 3.50-3.75% target, with consensus for roughly 3.00-3.25% by end-2026 -- so DGS2 steps down slowly and predictably. (b) The long end is held up by a positive and rising term premium sourced from fiscal supply: $2T+ annual deficits plus balance-sheet runoff force private absorption of a growing share of long-dated paper against foreign official demand that has plateaued since 2014, so DGS10 does not follow the front end down. The result is a normalization that is explicitly mid-course rather than finished: 2s10s un-inverted in Sep 2024, only achieved a sustained positive slope across tenors in Q4 2025, and sat at roughly 42bp on 2026-08-04 (DGS2 4.21%, DGS10 4.63%) -- still well below the 100-150bp range typical of a normal expansion. curve_carry trend-follows this slope with a DV01-neutral TLT/IEF position, so the only real choice here is which timescale of slope change the signal measures. Both prior pipeline curve_carry proposals sample the short end of the pre-registered range (63d, 126d), which resolves the FOMC/CPI/auction repricing sitting ON TOP of the normalization rather than the normalization itself; 252d -- the top of the range -- measures slope change over a full year, matching the clock of the two drivers above. Monthly rebalance is the honest turnover match for a signal whose sign at a 252d lookback changes on a quarters-to-years cadence. Proposed as a structural hypothesis about a mechanism and its timescale, not from any claim about slope trades' recent results -- a year-scale slope trend this widely narrated may well already be priced, which is what the OOS gate is for.

The ticker's dominant fundamental driver has therefore CHANGED -- from broad EM growth/commodity/currency beta to the capacity cycle of the AI semiconductor supply chain -- and that is a composition fact checkable from holdings data, not a view. MECHANISM. A trailing-sign rule monetizes something only when the asset's dominant driver is serially correlated. Contracted manufacturing capacity is serially correlated by industrial construction rather than by sentiment: DRAM capacity is reported effectively sold out through 2026 and into 2027, and TSMC lifted its 2026 capex plan to $60-64bn from $52-56bn. Underneath sits the textbook slow-adjusting capital stock -- a leading-edge fab takes roughly 2-3 years to build -- so the industry's capacity/price cycle over- and under-shoots on a multi-year clock. That persistence is symmetric: an over-capacity downswing is as slow as an upswing, which is why this is a persistence claim and not a bullish one. The concentration that gives the driver its persistence also makes this a single-supply-chain bet wearing an EM label: a Taiwan/Korea geopolitical event, an export-control change, or one company's process failure would dominate the signal, and none of those are serially correlated at all -- the diversification the 'EM' label implies is largely gone, and that concentration is itself being flagged as an index-level risk. name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_TLT_GLD_126_189
rationale: STRUCTURAL COMPOSITION, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM. I assert nothing about how trend signals, gold, long Treasuries, or any live strategy has recently performed; a trailing-sign rule takes BOTH directions on each leg, so nothing here forecasts a direction for either. THE SPECIFIC MECHANISM MAKING THESE TWO LEGS OFFSET (v1.14 requires a named one, not an uncorrelatedness claim): official-sector reserve substitution. Long-dated Treasuries and gold are the two dominant instruments in the same balance sheet -- global official FX reserves -- and a reallocation between them mechanically removes demand from one leg and adds it to the other. That reallocation is documented and large: gold overtook US Treasuries as the world's second-largest official reserve asset by end-2025 (gold's share of official reserves 20% in 2024 -> 27% in 2025, Treasuries down to 22%), central banks bought a net 244 tonnes in Q1 2026 alone, and 74% of reserve managers surveyed expect moderate-to-significantly lower USD reserve holdings over the next five years. The Treasury side of that same shift is visible as a price: the NY Fed ACM 10y term premium is positive for the first time since 2023 and topped 50bp for the first time since 2014, with the long end the most exposed point on the curve precisely because the price-insensitive foreign official bid was concentrated there -- 30y ~5.15-5.20% against a 10y ~4.6% that touched an 18-month high of ~4.75% this week, and $2T+ annual deficits keeping issuance at the 20y/30y points heavy. So the driver of the TLT leg right now is sovereign supply and issuer risk, not growth or inflation expectations. WHY THIS IS A REGIME-DEPENDENT RELATIONSHIP, WHICH IS THE SHAPE THIS PRIMITIVE'S CORRELATION GUARD ACTUALLY WANTS. When the long end is driven by growth scares, TLT and GLD are substitutes and rally together (positive relationship). When it is driven by fiscal supply and issuer risk -- the current regime, per the term-premium evidence above -- gold absorbs exactly the sovereign-risk hedging demand that long Treasuries shed, and the relationship inverts. A relationship that flips sign across regimes is what can carry a real economic mechanism while still clearing an unconditional |corr| <= 0.3 cap; a permanently offsetting pair could not. PARAMETERIZATION, MATCHED TO EACH DRIVER'S OWN CLOCK. lookback_a=126 (~6 months) on TLT spans two consecutive quarterly refunding cycles, so the leg's sign reflects the supply/term-premium impulse rather than one auction or one CPI print. lookback_b=189 (~9 months, three quarters) on GLD matches the cadence at which official reserve accumulation is actually decided and reported (quarterly WGC/IMF reserve data, annual allocation mandates) -- deliberately SLOWER than the rates leg, which no prior asset_class_trend_hedge draw here has done (252/252, 252/60, 252/63, 189/63 all run the second leg at or faster than the first). Monthly rebalance is the honest turnover match for two multi-quarter signals under v1.5's duty-cycle-matched null. VOCABULARY BREADTH: asset_class_trend_hedge is tied for least-used in this ledger (4 of 28 rows), TLT+GLD is an untested leg pair here, and graveyard.csv contains no TLT/GLD row of any kind. WHAT CUTS AGAINST IT, STATED BEFORE THE RESULT IS KNOWN. (1) The mechanism I cite is largely POST-2022 (sanctions, reserve fragmentation, the fiscal-supply regime), while the calibration window that screens this candidate is 2007-2017 -- an era when TLT and GLD were both QE/disinflation beneficiaries. Their calibration-window trend signs may well correlate above CALIB_CORR_CAP=0.3 and get this mechanically rejected. I am not asserting it passes; the guard exists to decide that, and a rejection here would be a correct outcome, not a defect in the proposal. (2) v1.14 names the real hazard directly: two zero-edge trend legs can look like they earn their place through variance reduction alone. Nothing in this rationale is evidence either leg has an edge. (3) Prior probability is low on this lab's own record -- 139+ strategies tested, 0 ALIVE predictive, and four sibling asset_class_trend_hedge rows already rest on related cross-class arguments.

name: rp_pair_zscore_HYG_LQD_90_2p0_4p0
rationale: US credit enters August 2026 at a historic tightness extreme: high-yield index OAS is ~281bp, inside the richest decile of its history against a long-run median near 450bp, while investment grade sits at ~81bp -- and the HY/IG ratio is near its long-run ~3.5x, i.e. the richness is market-wide rather than a quality-tier distortion. That is a structural asymmetry in the HYG-vs-LQD relative price, not a directional view: with HY already in its richest decile there is very little remaining spread-compression headroom for HYG to keep grinding richer against LQD, while the widening episodes that do occur are sharp and are pulled back by HY's much larger carry -- a bounded, snap-back distribution is exactly the shape a z-scored log-spread mean-reversion signal is built for, and the opposite of the one-way drift that kills this primitive on a trending ratio. Two current conditions reinforce it. (1) Rate volatility is dormant (MOVE ~75, having touched ~59 in late 2025), so the HYG/LQD duration mismatch (HYG ~3yr vs LQD ~8yr) injects less rates noise into the log-spread than in a high-rate-vol regime -- the spread is closer to a pure credit-quality signal now than it usually is. (2) Investment-grade gross supply is forecast at ~$2.25tn for 2026, a ~35% YoY increase that could outpace demand for the first time since 2022 -- an identified LQD-specific pressure, i.e. a source of relative dislocation for the ratio to revert from rather than a trend either leg should ride. Deliberately NOT the always-on long-HY carry bet already proposed as rp_static_spread_carry_HYG_LQD_a (2026-08-04): at the richest decile an always-on structural bet is the worst-priced version of this trade, which is precisely why the dislocate-and-revert shape is the one worth testing. z_window=90 (~4.5 months) spans a full credit-spread dislocation cycle rather than a single risk-off week; entry 2.0 / stop 4.0 keeps the standard band this primitive's earlier proposals used; weekly rebalance because credit-ETF relative dislocations resolve over weeks, and this is the first pair_zscore proposal at a frequency other than daily, where turnover cost dominates a spread trade. Structural/valuation reasoning only -- no claim about any strategy's recent performance.

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_momentum_63_3
rationale: Cross-asset return dispersion is at a genuine structural extreme in 2026, and it is wide across exactly the asset classes UNIVERSE spans rather than inside any single one. Concrete instances: the gold/oil ratio sits near 55 (early-2026 readings ~75:1 with gold ~$5,000/oz against oil ~$67/bbl) versus a since-1900 average near 20 and a modern average ~22 -- the far right tail of its whole historical distribution, matched only by April 2020 and the 1980s oil crises; 2026 asset-class performance spans roughly +94.5% (silver) to -20% (natural gas); and fixed income's own 2026 theme is explicitly dispersion 'across sectors, structures, and parts of the curve' rather than a uniform beta-driven opportunity set. Cboe's DSPX implied-dispersion index independently hit a 6-year high of 47% in the week of 2026-07-13, above its April 'Liberation Day' peak -- that one measures single-stock dispersion inside SPY, not cross-asset dispersion, so it is corroborating context here, not the load-bearing fact. Why this matters mechanically for THIS primitive and not as a performance claim: a cross-sectional long-short's gross payoff is the top-K minus bottom-K return spread, which scales directly with the dispersion of the cross-section it ranks. Wide dispersion does not make the ranking correct -- it raises the payoff per unit of ranking accuracy, and equally the loss per unit of ranking error. That is the structural condition; whether momentum ranking has any accuracy at all is precisely what the doctrine's gates are being asked to decide. Why momentum as the metric, and why 63 days: the same 2026 research describes elevated structural breaks across many cross-asset pairs simultaneously (gold rising alongside real yields, the gold/oil ratio at a multi-decade extreme) -- a regime in which each asset is driven by its own idiosyncratic, slow-moving macro driver (central-bank and ETF gold demand, Treasury term premium and supply, an oil supply shock followed by ceasefire reversal) rather than by a common factor. Persistent asset-specific drivers are the structural precondition for the rank ordering itself to persist, which is all cross-sectional momentum bets on. 63 days is the short end of the standard 3-12 month formation window, chosen because the drivers above are turning over fast in a regime transition -- deliberately distinct from the two momentum draws this pipeline has already proposed (126/k=2 on 2026-08-05, 252/k=4 on 2026-08-06); this is a different formation horizon pre-registered on its own reasoning, not a re-run of either. k=3 of 15 tickers keeps both sleeves diversified within an asset class rather than concentrating the whole position in whichever single commodity is at an extreme. Monthly rebalance because a 63-day formation does not justify paying weekly or daily turnover. Honest prior: this lab has already killed cross-sectional momentum (2 graveyard rows under xsec_momentum) and 52 low_vol_xsec rows besides, and no predictive strategy here has ever survived. name: rp_static_spread_carry_SLV_GLD_a
rationale: Silver and gold share nearly all of their monetary drivers -- real rates, the dollar, ETF and central-bank demand -- so a fixed long-SLV/short-GLD spread nets those out and leaves one exposure standing: silver's industrial demand and its physical supply balance. That balance is structural, not cyclical noise. The Silver Institute / Metals Focus World Silver Survey 2026 (published 2026-04-15) puts 2026 at a SIXTH consecutive annual market deficit of 46.3 Moz, up 15% from 40.3 Moz in 2025, and the deficit is widening even though total demand is forecast to fall ~2% -- because mine and scrap supply are falling faster (~-2%). Cumulatively 762 Moz has been drawn from above-ground stocks since 2021, so the inventory buffer absorbing the gap is finite and measurably smaller each year. Industrial use ran ~680 Moz in 2024, roughly 60% of total demand, with solar PV alone at ~120-125 Moz against a 665 GW 2026 install forecast. That industrial share is precisely the risk being borne, and it is why this is a carry bet rather than a forecast: the long leg carries a real industrial and solar-capex cycle that the short leg does not, and it gets punished hard when that cycle turns -- the gold-silver ratio sat above 100 as recently as 2025 before trading in the ~55-65 range in 2026, which is the drawdown scale this spread can inflict, not a reason to expect it to keep going. The proposal rests on the deficit and the demand mix, not on the recent direction of the ratio. Monthly rebalance because the position has no timing content at all -- it is always-on, and the only turnover is drift correction. Distinct from rp_pair_zscore_GLD_SLV_60_2p0_4p0 (proposed 2026-08-05), which tests this same spread as MEAN-REVERSION around its own rolling mean; this is a bet on the spread's level, the same distinction rp_static_spread_carry_TLT_IEF_a drew against family N's cointegration row. No SLV/GLD static spread appears anywhere in graveyard.csv or pipeline_ideas.csv.

name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_TLT_UUP_189_63
rationale: A bear-steepening regime has structurally SPLIT the two ends of the US curve, and TLT and UUP are driven by opposite ends of that split -- so their trend legs are driven by different economic segments, not by one shared factor. Long end: the 30s2s spread went 81 -> 99bp in the five sessions to 2026-07-27, and yields past 15y are held above 5% by term premium, Treasury supply and long-run inflation expectations rather than by the expected policy path -- a multi-quarter repricing, hence lookback_a=189 on the rates leg. Front end: short-rate support for the dollar is fading on softening US data (Q2 2026 real GDP 1.5%, June payrolls +57k, core CPI 2.6% from a 4.2% May headline), the 2s10s has re-steepened to about +35bp with effective funds at 3.63%, and DXY sits near 99.5 at a seven-week low with a widened $77.6bn May trade deficit and reserve managers cutting USD holdings -- a repricing that has turned over roughly a quarter, hence lookback_b=63 on the currency leg. The named offsetting mechanism this primitive requires: TLT's trend is a LONG-end term-premium/supply process while UUP's trend is a SHORT-end relative-policy-rate process, and in a steepener those two segments move apart by construction -- the leg that is a duration bet is not implicitly a dollar bet. New to this pipeline on both counts: UUP has never appeared as a leg of asset_class_trend_hedge (prior legs: SPY/GLD, TLT/DBC, SPY/IEF, VNQ/DBC, TLT/GLD), and the primitive has never paired rates against currency. Monthly rebalance because both lookbacks are quarterly-to-multiquarter; under DOCTRINE v1.5b's duty-cycle-matched null a slow signal should not be traded faster than it actually changes.
